output.summary: KEP-3960 adds a built-in sleep action to the PreStop lifecycle hook, letting a container pause for a set duration before termination. The KEP reached stage stable and is marked implemented.
output.rationale:
Exec-based sleep requires a sleep binary in the image, and the KEP argues sleep should be a first-class feature. A preStop delay gives load balancers and kube-proxy time to stop routing to a terminating pod before the container receives SIGTERM. The status history shows implementable from 2023-06-16 and implemented from 2025-09-19.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Run sleep via exec in the preStop hook (e.g. command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 20"])
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this "requires a sleep binary in the image. We should offer sleep as a first-class thing."

alternatives.option: Rely on the Terminating endpoint state alone, without a sleep
alternatives.why_not: A commenter notes that load balancers have their own sync loops and may still route to a pod that has received SIGTERM, so sleep remains used. The sources do not record a formal rejection of this option.

alternatives.option: Mark the container NOT READY while the sleep runs
alternatives.why_not: thockin argued this could harm reliability for low-N services because kube-proxy-terminating-endpoints only considers ready pods, giving the example of a pod with externalTrafficPolicy Local.
Raised in comment 2209320166 as a possible extension requiring a feature gate and a short KEP. The sources do not show it was adopted.

evidence.quote: We propose adding a new sleep action for the PreStop hook, which will pause the container for a specified duration before termination.
Another way to run `sleep` in a container is to use `exec` command in `preStop hook` like `command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 20"]`. However, this requires a sleep binary in the image.
Adding a sleep is the de facto solution. This moves 4a ("nginx receives SIGTERM") out in time past the LB data-plane programming.
Given that this KEP has graduated to `stable`, if all the work is completed, could you please update the KEP status in `kep.yaml` to `implemented`, and then close this issue?
Looks like the code was reverted as part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128627 due to test flakes and the KEP is no longer targeting stable for v1.32 release.
